lead.title: Atlas Bio emerges in Basel with $12.5M (seed led by Creandum) to simulate patient response and lighten Phase 2 trials
lead.deck: Founded by Simon Romanski (CEO) and Sebastian Bayer (CTO), the Basel startup trains a foundation model on about 2 million human RNA readouts to predict how patient profiles respond to different treatments — choosing diseases, subpopulations and trial design. It already works with a top-10 pharma; the idea that simulation can replace Phase 2 trials remains unproven for now.

milestone.title: Immatics presents PRAME data at ESMO 2026: 25% confirmed responses for engager IMA402, 41% for TCR-T IMA203CD8
milestone.summary: In 40 patients at the recommended dose, bispecific engager IMA402 shows a 25% confirmed objective response rate (32% in high-PRAME); personalized TCR-T IMA203CD8 reaches 41% in 90 evaluable patients, 55% in gynecologic tumors at relevant doses. Uncontrolled Phase 1b data — read with caution.
milestone.why: PRAME is a solid "shared" target across tumor types: the results feed the TCR-T / engager thesis in solid tumors, with first IMA402 + IMA401 lung data expected in 2027.

deal.thesis: Swiss Ferring acquires New York-based Gameto for up to $1.3825B including milestones (upfront undisclosed): Fertilo, lab-based egg maturation using iPSC-derived cells, is in Phase 3 (500 participants) and cuts the two weeks of hormone injections of classic IVF. A comparable for femtech biotech.

brefsEurope.title: CasZyme teams up with Cirena to optimize long guide RNAs for its Cas12l nuclease
brefsEurope.summary: The Lithuanian nuclease engineer will test 150–170 nt synthetic guides in primary T cells; editing-efficiency results expected early 2027, financial terms undisclosed.

word.fr: T cells armed with a TCR
word.definition: The patient's T cells are collected, given a receptor (TCR) that recognizes a fragment of a tumor protein displayed by cancer cells, then reinfused.

parts.label: Peptide-HLA
parts.role: the target displayed on the tumor surface

how.t: T cells are collected from the patient by leukapheresis.
A TCR targeting a tumor peptide (e.g. PRAME) is introduced into the cells, which are then expanded.
The modified cells recognize and destroy tumor cells expressing the target.

word.why: Unlike CAR-T, TCR-T sees intracellular targets, hence solid-tumor potential; the VC question is patient selection (HLA, target expression) and manufacturing cost.
